blocks.text:
I'm scanning chain A and chain B coordinates to identify residues in close proximity, comparing their spatial ranges to narrow down which chain A residues (like PRO 6, LYS 7, PHE 9, LEU 65) have y-coordinates overlapping with chain B's range.

I'm working through chain B residues one by one—ASP 239, GLU 240, ASP 241, VAL 242—checking their coordinates against nearby chain A atoms to see if any fall within the 4.0 Å threshold, but so far these early B residues don't seem close enough to any chain A atoms.

Now I'm shifting focus to later chain B residues like TRP 245, TRP 253, and ILE 257, which have different coordinates that might land closer to chain A. To check this systematically, I'm compiling a list of chain A atoms with y-coordinates below -4, since chain B's minimum y is around -6, starting with PRO6's CA and CB positions.

I'm continuing that same list, now noting LYS7's backbone and side chain atoms (N through NZ) along with its carbonyl oxygen, and beginning to check ALA8's nitrogen position for similar y-value criteria.

Still logging coordinates...

Still recording atomic coordinates...

Still recording atomic coordinates...

Still checking coordinates for TYR78's ring atoms, then scanning LYS118's side chain positions and confirming ASP119 has no atoms below y=-4 besides the carbonyl oxygen.

Continuing through the residue coordinates: ASP119's carboxylate group sits around y=-5 to -6, then I'm tracking LYS120, ILE121, and GLU122's backbone and side chain atom positions.

Still logging coordinate data...

Now I'm scanning chain B coordinates residue by residue, checking distances against candidate chain A residues to find matching contact regions—like comparing B242's VAL CG2 position to LYS7's CE atom to see if they're close enough to indicate an interaction.

CG2-CE comes out to 3.79 Å, confirming B242 VAL is within range, so I'll include it. Now I'm checking B241 ASP's atom coordinates against LYS7 to see if it also falls within the distance cutoff.

Checking B241 ASP against nearby chain A atoms, but the distance to LYS7 NZ is about 6.1 Å, too far, so it's excluded. Moving to B243 LYS, none of its atoms are close enough to chain A residues like PRO6 either, so I'm ruling that out too, and now checking B244 LYS.

Now I'm checking B245 TRP's coordinates against chain A candidates near LYS7 and CYS58 to see if any fall within contact range.

Checking LYS7 side chain atoms against TRP245 CB shows too large a y-distance to be a real contact, so I'm ruling that pairing out. Now I'm scanning other chain A residues like ILE61 and GLU62 for proximity, but those don't fit either, so I keep searching nearby residues for the actual interface contact.

That doesn't seem to work either. Let me check ARG246's coordinates against the LYS7 region to see if any atoms fall within contact range.

Actually, stepping back - chain B is a helix stretching across a wide x/y/z range while chain A forms a compact globular domain, so I need to compare their overall spatial ranges to find where they could plausibly touch.

I'm scanning chain B residues with y-values above -12, since that's the zone closest to chain A, checking each atom's coordinates in residues 242, 245, 246, and 249 for potential contact points.

Still recording atom coordinates...

Still recording atomic coordinates...

Still recording atom coordinates...

With the coordinate scan finished, I'm now grouping chain A's candidate atoms by spatial region to check for potential contacts—separating lysine and leucine side chains, then the histidine and proline/leucine/cysteine cluster near the interface.

Continuing on, I'm mapping out further regions covering glutamate through asparagine, the isoleucine-to-aspartate cluster, and a tyrosine hydroxyl group nearby. I'm then cross-referencing an arginine's beta and gamma carbons against chain A atoms in the same coordinate range to spot phenylalanine, proline, and methionine residues that could sit close enough to interact.

I check the arginine's NH1 position against nearby chain A atoms but nothing lines up there, so this residue may not be making a direct contact. I then shift attention to a tryptophan positioned further out, scanning chain A for tyrosine, cysteine, and isoleucine residues that fall within its coordinate window to see if they're close enough to count as an interaction.

I find that isoleucine's CG2 atom sits about 3.6 angstroms from the tryptophan's CZ2 atom, confirming a genuine contact between the two chains. Now I'm cross-checking other nearby residues in that same region—lysine's CE, CD, and NZ atoms along with additional isoleucine and valine atoms—to see if they also fall within contact range.

I decide a more systematic approach is needed: I'll compile all chain A atoms with y-coordinates at or below -3, then work through each chain B residue methodically, checking distances against this filtered set of chain A atoms rather than jumping around.

I've confirmed a contact between VAL242 and LYS7 at roughly 3.79 Å. Now I'm examining TRP245's coordinates against nearby chain A atoms in that spatial region, checking LYS7's side chain atoms and LEU65's beta carbon for potential proximity.

Distances I'm calculating come out to roughly 5.0-5.6 Å between TRP245's CB and LYS7's CG, so I'm continuing to check other atom pairs like TRP245 CD1 against LYS7 CB to find the closest actual contact.

I'm ruling out several candidates - LEU65's O, PRO68's CG, and LEU67's CB all sit too far from TRP245's NE1 position, so I'm still hunting for whichever chain A atom lies nearest that coordinate cluster.

Checking LYS7's oxygen against TRP245's NE1: the distance comes out to roughly 3.73 Å, which puts it within contact range. I'm verifying the coordinate against the source atom record to confirm this is correct.

I'm also checking TRP245's CD1 against the same LYS7 oxygen, but that distance is around 4.11 Å, just outside the cutoff. So B245 counts as a contact overall. Now I'm scanning nearby chain A atoms in that region to rule out other residues, then moving to examine ARG246's side chain atoms for potential proximity.

Checking the distance between ARG246 NH1 and PRO6 O gives about 2.82 Å, confirming a contact, so B246 is included. Now I'm pulling coordinates for B247 GLU's backbone and side chain atoms to continue mapping nearby residues.

Both B247 and B248 GLU residues stay at y values below -12, well outside range of chain A's closest atoms near x -3, z 9, so neither shows contact. I'm now checking B249 ARG's atom coordinates for potential proximity.

Continuing the coordinate scan, I find ARG249's CD atom sits only 3.73 Å from PRO68's CB on chain A, confirming a genuine contact once I verify the PRO68 coordinates match. That distance falls under the 4 Å threshold, so B249 counts as a contact, while its CG atom stays too far. Now I'm moving on to check LYS250's backbone atoms for similar proximity.

I don't find a match against PHE9's CG or LEU125's various sidechain atoms nearest chain A - the distances to NZ from CD1 and CG on LEU125 all exceed 4 Å, and the closest I get is LEU125's O atom at roughly 4.1 Å from NZ, just barely missing the cutoff.

Then checking LEU125's backbone C atom against NZ of LYS B250 gives 3.14 Å — that's a real contact, confirming B250 makes contact with chain A. Moving to LYS B251, I check its backbone and sidechain atoms (N, CA, C, O, CB) but all sit at y ≤ -13.9, too far from anything on chain A to register.

For MET B252, none of its atoms come close enough to chain A residues like CYS71 or TYR78 — the y-coordinate gap is too large, so no contact there either. TRP B253 does show a genuine contact with ILE121's CG2 at 3.60 Å. Now I'm pulling coordinates for LEU B254 to check its proximity next.

Checking LEU254's CD2 against GLU122's CG on chain A, the distance comes out to roughly 3.97 Å — just barely within the 4.0 Å contact threshold, so this looks like a real contact worth confirming with a precise recalculation.

Now I'm moving on to checking LEU255's coordinates for potential contacts as well.

Checking LYS256's atom coordinates next for any close proximity to the ligand.

Checking the distance between B256's carbon and ASN75's ND2 atom - working out dx, dy, dz gives about 3.77 Å, which counts as a contact.

Also checking O to ND2 distance - around 2.77 Å, another confirmed contact.

Now I'm pulling coordinates for ILE B257's backbone and side chain atoms to run through the same contact analysis.

Checking against nearby chain A residues: CYS71's oxygen is too far (>4 Å), but LYS118's NZ atom comes in at 2.96 Å from B257's oxygen, confirming that contact. I'm also checking TYR78's CE1 ring carbon against CD1 of the isoleucine side chain.

Now checking B258 SER contacts: LYS118's NZ is too far at 4.30 Å, but GLU122's OE1 comes in close at 2.21 Å to the serine's OG hydroxyl, confirming another contact.

Moving to B259 ASN, I'm computing coordinates for its backbone and side chain atoms, then checking distances to GLU122's OE1, CD, and OE2 in chain A to look for potential contacts there too.

Checking LYS118 NZ and ASP119 OD1 against B259's N and ND2, most fall just outside the 4.0 threshold except ASP119's OD1 to ND2, which comes in around 3.08 — a valid contact.

I'm also confirming ASP119 OD1 to CG at roughly 3.85, another contact. Then I move on to B260 ASN, laying out its coordinates and checking distances against GLU122 and ASP119 on chain A.

ND2 to GLU122 OE2 comes out to about 3.73, confirming a contact, so B260 is included in the interface list. I double-check the N atom against OE2 but that distance exceeds 4, ruling it out.

Now I'm working through B261 LYS, listing its backbone and side chain coordinates and starting to compare them against nearby chain A residues like GLU122 and LYS118 to check for additional contacts.

I calculate the distance between LYS261's NZ and ASN75's ND2 on chain A: dx=3.813, dy=-0.538, dz=0.473, giving roughly 3.88, confirming another contact — so B261 also belongs in the interface set.

Moving to B262 GLN, I record its atom coordinates and start scanning chain A residues like ASN75, GLU122, and LYS111 for any close contacts.

For LYS111 CD, the y-coordinate is too far from B262's atoms, and no chain A residue near x~10-13 has y close to -12, so I rule out a contact for B262.

I then work through B263 LYS, checking its CE and NZ atoms against GLU122's OE2 and CD and against ASP119's OD2, but all distances exceed 4 Å, so B263 also shows no contact — prompting me to look for chain A atoms near y~-12 in a different x range, checking LEU125's C coordinate next.

The closest chain A oxygen is GLU122 OE2 at y=-11.07, still over 4.4 Å from B263's atoms, confirming no contact there either. I then move to B264 HIS and start pulling its backbone and side-chain coordinates to check against nearby chain A residues.

Checking B265's remaining atoms against chain A's GLU122 - the distance is too large, no contact there. I still need to go back and verify several residues I may have skipped over: B239, B240, B241, B243, B244, B247, B248, B251, B252, and B255.

Let me look more closely at B243 and B244 since they're near LYS7/PRO6. B243's LYS coordinates don't put it close enough to chain A's PRO6 region to count as contact.

B244 also stays too far in y-coordinate to qualify. I'm moving on to check B239 and B240 next.

B239's coordinates place it too far from any chain A residue, and B240 similarly shows no proximity. B241's ASP residue also comes up too distant from LYS7, so I'm ruling that out too and continuing to B248-B250.

I'm rechecking B247's minimum y-position residue against nearby chain A atoms like PHE9, finding it's still too far (6.9 apart), then moving to examine B252's coordinates for its minimum y positions.

Testing GLU72's CG against MET252's CB gives a distance of about 3.80, which registers as a genuine contact—worth flagging.

Now I'm being more systematic, pulling together all chain A atoms with y-coordinates below -8 to check against the chain B helix core, starting with PHE9's aromatic ring atoms and LEU69's backbone and sidechain positions.

Continuing through GLU72 and ASP73 to build out coordinates for the acidic residues in this region.

Recording coordinates for ASN75 and marking LEU69 finished, then moving to GLU122's atom positions.

GLU72 OE1 sits around y -11.098. Now moving to reconcile chain B residues against this expanded chain A coordinate set, starting with B247 GLU whose atoms span roughly y -12.6.

For B248 GLU I'm checking distances against nearby chain A candidates in the x -3 to -6, y -9 to -12, z 3-6 window, but nothing lands close enough to count as contact.

I'm now moving to LYS251, checking its backbone and side chain coordinates out to NZ for potential nearby chain A atoms.

Chain A's GLU72 is still too far to form a contact there, so I'll move on to LEU255 and start pulling its coordinates.

Checking B255 distances again - the GLU72 CG position is too far from B255's carbon, ruling that out. I'm now re-examining B262's atom coordinates against chain A's positions near x=10-12 to see if anything falls within contact range.

Testing B263's CD atom against GLU122's OE2 - the delta values are too large for a real contact, so B263 is excluded. Checking ASP119's OD1 y-coordinate against B263's y-range confirms no overlap either, and B265 also shows no contact.

I've verified B239 through B246 already, and now I'm going through B242 again along with the remaining unchecked residues: B249, B250, B252-B254, and B256-B261, to make sure I haven't missed any real contacts.

Compiling the final list of contacting residues gives me 242, 245, 246, 249, 250, 252-254, 256-261, and 264, while 239-241, 243-244, 247-248, 251, 255, 262-263, and 265 are excluded. The pattern looks consistent with one helix face making contact roughly every 3-4 residues, though a few like 254, 258, and 259 are borderline cases I need to double-check against the actual PDB coordinates.

Checking B254's LEU CD2 against GLU122's CG using the raw coordinate data, the distance comes out to 3.973 - just within the 4.0 cutoff, confirming this is a real contact.

I verify B252's MET CB to GLU72's CG distance at 3.798, B249's ARG CD to PRO68's CB at 3.733, and now I'm working out the B250 LYS NZ to LEU125 C distance using the coordinate differences.

Continuing through the contact list, I confirm several more residues fall within range: B245's TRP NE1 to LYS7's O at 3.729, B246's ARG NH1 to PRO6's O at 2.82, B242's VAL CG2 to LYS7's CE at 3.791, and B253 at 3.60. I then check B256 through B261, finding contacts to ASN75, LYS118, GLU122, ASP119, and again ASN75, with distances ranging from 2.21 to 3.88, and I'm now double-checking that last one against ASN75's ND2 coordinates.

Confirming the distance comes out to 3.880, so it's in range, and I move on to check B264's NE2 to GLU122 OE2 at 2.52. I then go back to verify a few residues previously marked as having no contacts—B243, B244, and checking other atoms of B247, B251, and B255 against nearby chain A atoms like GLU72's OE2 and TYR78's OH—confirming these are too far to count.

I continue through B262, B263, B265, and B239-241, finding no contacts in chain A within range. Then I check whether I've missed any chain A regions near chain B residues 239-241, comparing extreme coordinates like LYS7's NZ against B241's CB, finding they're about 6 units apart—too far, so I move to check other chain A residues in that region.

Checking CYS58 and GLU59 near B240 also comes up empty, as does B244. I re-verify B248 against the PRO68 region and find no contact, then plan to systematically scan through all chain A atoms for y-values below -6 to make sure I haven't missed any potential contacts.

Working through chain A residue by residue, PHE9's ring carbons dip into that y-range, but PRO4 through PRO10 otherwise stay above the threshold. I continue scanning residues 11 through 57, most of which have positive y-coordinates, and start checking LEU44's side chain position.

Continuing through the coordinate scan: HIS66 shows its lowest y around -5.609 at the O atom, LEU67's O sits at -4.544, and PRO68 has y-values ranging near -7.427 for O down to -4.682 for N. LEU69 and LEU70 both show fairly negative y-coordinates across their backbone and side chain atoms, clustering around -6 to -10, and I'm now checking CYS71's atoms which start near -6 to -7.5.

I keep tracking minimum y-values atom by atom: GLU72's side chain reaches down to about -11.098 at OE1, LYS74 and ASN75 stay in the -6 to -11 range, and VAL76/PRO77 hover closer to -2 to -5. Moving into TYR78 and jumping ahead to TYR115, I notice TYR115's OH atom has a notably low y of -7.161, which stands out as a potential minimum before ALA116 shows values closer to zero.

Now I'm working through VAL117, LYS118, and their backbone/sidechain coordinates, trying to pin down exact N, CA, C, O positions for each residue as I scan the atom listing.

Continuing through THR123's remaining atoms and LEU124-125 coordinates, I'm noting a potential interesting proximity between TYR115's OH and something in chain B, possibly ASN260's OD1 -- worth checking if these residues are close enough to interact across chains.

Checking further, I'm ruling out several candidate contacts: LYS263 NZ is too far, THR123's oxygen is far from chain B, and comparing GLU248's CB against LEU69's side chain shows no proximity. I'm also checking B255 against GLU72/ASN75 and B251 against GLU72 for possible contacts, finding nothing new so far.

Verifying ARG246's NH1 against PRO6's oxygen confirms a real contact within cutoff. Compiling the confirmed contact list: V242, W245, R246, R249, K250, M252, W253, L254, K256, I257, S258, N259, N260, K261, H264 — though I still want to double-check the borderline cases at B248, B255, and B262.
